extracted.intended_audience: Authors, editors, reviewers and other stakeholders involved in biomedical/medical journal publishing
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for the conduct, reporting, editing, and publication of scholarly work in medical journals (ICMJE recommendations), aimed at helping authors, editors and reviewers produce and handle accurate, clear, reproducible, and unbiased articles and to follow appropriate reporting standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best practices and ethical standards in conduct and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Review best practices and ethical standards in the conduct and reporting of research and other material published in medical journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The recommendations are intended to guide authors, editors, and others involved in peer review and biomedical publishing on ethical and best-practice matters throughout the research and publication lifecycle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article quality: accuracy, clarity, reproducibility and lack of bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Help authors, editors, and others involved in peer review and biomedical publishing to create, review and distribute accurate, clear, reproducible, unbiased medical journal articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuscripts should be checked and handled so that published material is factually accurate, clearly communicated, sufficiently detailed to allow reproducibility where appropriate, and free from undue bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of tailored reporting guidelines for specific study types
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should also use tailored guidelines for reporting of specific study types (e.g., the CONSORT guidelines for the reporting of randomized trials).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing manuscripts, authors are expected to follow applicable reporting checklists and standards (CONSORT, STROBE, PRISMA, etc.) relevant to their study design to ensure completeness and transparency of reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow individual journals' instructions in addition to ICMJE
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should use these recommendations along with individual journals’ instructions to authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ICMJE recommendations are a baseline; authors must also adhere to any additional or variant requirements specified by the target journal (formatting, submission procedures, policies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of hands-on guidance for journals, reviewers and editors on publication responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: These recommendations give journals, reviewers and editors hands-on guidance on how to deal with their specific responsibilities in the publication process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors and reviewers should consult the recommendations for practical guidance on tasks such as handling submissions, managing peer review, addressing ethical concerns, and making publication decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journals: adopt and declare adherence to ICMJE recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Journals that follow these recommendations are encouraged to incorporate them into their instructions to authors and to make explicit in those instructions that they follow ICMJE recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journals should embed ICMJE-based requirements into author-facing policies and clearly state compliance so authors understand expected standards; note that ICMJE does not enforce compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intended primary audience and voluntary uptake
rubrics_metrics.description: These recommendations are intended primarily for use by authors who might submit their work for publication to the International Committee of Medical Journal Editors (ICMJE)’s member journals; many non-ICMJE journals voluntarily use these recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users should understand that the recommendations serve as widely accepted guidance but may be adopted voluntarily by journals outside the ICMJE membership; always check specific journal policy for applicability.
